arnalforne2024dermis.cite: Arnal-Forné M, Molina-García T, Ortega M, et al.. Changes in human skin composition due to intrinsic aging: a histologic and morphometric study. Histochemistry and Cell Biology. 2024;162:259–271.
arnalforne2024dermis.what: With intrinsic ageing the papillary (not the reticular) dermis becomes thicker; total cellularity and vascularisation fall in both.

assi2024asian.cite: Ali A, Colombe L, Mélanie P, et al.. Comparison of facial skin ageing in healthy Asian and Caucasian females quantified by in vivo line‐field confocal optical coherence tomography 3D imaging. Skin Research and Technology. 2024;30:e13643.
assi2024asian.what: LC-OCT of 109 Asian women aged 20–70 years in China against 100 Caucasian women of the same method in France: at the cheekbone the viable epidermis is 15.4 % and the stratum corneum 9.6 % thicker on average across the age groups; at the temple and the mandible only in two and one of five age groups.

belyakov2005skin.cite: Belyakov OV, Mitchell SA, Parikh D, et al.. Biological effects in unirradiated human tissue induced by radiation damage up to 1 mm away. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 2005;102:14203–14208.
belyakov2005skin.what: In a 3D normal human tissue model, unirradiated cells up to 1 mm from irradiated cells showed more micronuclei (1.7-fold) and apoptosis (2.8-fold).

bonnier2023lcoct.cite: Bonnier F, Pedrazzani M, Fischman S, et al.. Line-field confocal optical coherence tomography coupled with artificial intelligence algorithms to identify quantitative biomarkers of facial skin ageing. Scientific Reports. 2023;13:13881.
bonnier2023lcoct.what: LC-OCT with artificial intelligence in 100 healthy Caucasian women aged 20–70 years at the temple, cheekbone and mandible: the comparison cohort of the Asian study.

boone2015hdoct.cite: Boone MALM, Suppa M, Marneffe A, et al.. High-definition optical coherence tomography intrinsic skin ageing assessment in women: a pilot study. Archives of Dermatological Research. 2015;307:705–720.
boone2015hdoct.what: HD-OCT of the inner upper arm (sun-protected) of 60 fair-skinned women, 20 per age group: the papillary dermis (valley of the DEJ to the second intensity peak) measured 63.75 ± 3.75, 54.75 ± 2.51 and 30.75 ± 1.19 µm at 20–39, 40–59 and 60–79 y.

branchet1990thickness.cite: Branchet MC, Boisnic S, Frances C, et al.. Skin thickness changes in normal aging skin. Gerontology. 1990;36:28–35.
branchet1990thickness.what: Histology of the upper inner arm, 34 women and 30 men aged 20–80: epidermal thickness 61.85 − 0.40 × age µm (r = −0.565), total dermal thickness falling by 12.8 µm per year (r = −0.473), about 6 % of the extrapolated zero-age thickness per decade; the superficial dermis biphasic around 50 years.

braunger2024aging.cite: Braunger JM, Cammarata LV, Sornapudi TR, et al.. Transcriptional changes are tightly coupled to chromatin reorganization during cellular aging. Aging Cell. 2024;23:e14056.
braunger2024aging.what: RNA-seq of skin fibroblasts from 133 individuals aged 1 to 96 years: hierarchical clustering of the transcriptomes gives five age groups, 1–15, 16–26, 27–60, 61–85 and 86–96 years.

braverman1997microcirculation.cite: Braverman IM. The Cutaneous Microcirculation: Ultrastructure and Microanatomical Organization. Microcirculation. 1997;4:329–340.
braverman1997microcirculation.what: The cutaneous microcirculation is two horizontal plexuses, one 1–1.5 mm below the skin surface and the other at the dermal–subcutaneous junction, connected by ascending arterioles and descending venules.

brincat1985thickness.cite: Brincat M, Moniz CJ, Studd JWW, et al.. Long‐term effects of the menopause and sex hormones on skin thickness. BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology. 1985;92:256–259.
brincat1985thickness.what: Thigh skin collagen of 77 untreated postmenopausal women correlates with the years since the menopause (ρ = 0.38) and not with chronological age.

burton2011hmts.cite: Burton SA, Ng CY, Simmers R, et al.. Rapid Intradermal Delivery of Liquid Formulations Using a Hollow Microstructured Array. Pharmaceutical Research. 2011;28:31–40.
burton2011hmts.what: A hollow microneedle device of 1.27 cm² carries eighteen 500–900 µm microstructures with 10–40 µm cannulae; the 900 µm structures penetrated swine skin to 612 µm on average and the device delivered 300–1500 µL intradermally.

castelobranco1992hrt.cite: Castelo-Branco C, Duran M, González-Merlo J. Skin collagen changes related to age and hormone replacement therapy. Maturitas. 1992;15:113–119.
castelobranco1992hrt.what: Skin collagen per protein in abdominal biopsies of 76 women by decade of age: 117.2, 117.7, 119.6, 114.2 and 108.0 µg/mg from the 20s to the 60s; it falls beyond the 40s and after the menopause.

chan2018asian.cite: Chan IL, Cohen S, da Cunha MG, et al.. Characteristics and management of Asian skin. International Journal of Dermatology. 2019;58:131–143.
chan2018asian.what: Review of Asian skin: phototypes from type III to IV in Chinese and Japanese and type IV and V in Indian and Pakistani people.

chopra2015face.cite: Chopra K, Calva D, Sosin M, et al.. A Comprehensive Examination of Topographic Thickness of Skin in the Human Face. Aesthetic Surgery Journal. 2015;35:1007–1013.
chopra2015face.what: Punch biopsies of 39 facial subunits from ten cadaveric heads: facial epidermis 29.6 µm (posterior auricular) to 62.6 µm (upper lip), dermis 759 µm (upper medial eyelid) to 1969 µm (lower nasal sidewall).

coppe2008sasp.cite: Coppé JP, Patil CK, Rodier F, et al.. Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotypes Reveal Cell-Nonautonomous Functions of Oncogenic RAS and the p53 Tumor Suppressor. PLoS Biology. 2008;6:e301.
coppe2008sasp.what: Cells induced to senesce by genotoxic stress secrete many factors linked to inflammation and malignancy: the senescence-associated secretory phenotype.

cordeiro2020templates.cite: Cordeiro AS, Tekko IA, Jomaa MH, et al.. Two-Photon Polymerisation 3D Printing of Microneedle Array Templates with Versatile Designs: Application in the Development of Polymeric Drug Delivery Systems. Pharmaceutical Research. 2020;37:174.
cordeiro2020templates.what: Two-photon-polymerised microneedle templates of 900–1300 µm height, 300–500 µm base width and 100–500 µm interspacing: sharp conical and pyramidal needles inserted to 64–90 % of their height in skin models.

crisan2012ultrasound.cite: Crisan M, Lupsor M, Crisan D, et al.. Ultrasonographic assessment of skin structure according to age. Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology, and Leprology. 2012;78:519.
crisan2012ultrasound.what: 20 MHz ultrasound of 160 subjects in four age groups (under 20, 21–40, 41–60, 61–80 years) at the dorsal forearm, the medial arm and the cheekbone: the dermis is thickest at 21–40 years on all sites (dorsal forearm 1.209, 1.279, 1.256 and 1.220 mm), the epidermis at similar values.

denda1990facial.cite: Denda M, Takahashi M. Measurement of facial skin thickness by ultrasound method.. Journal of Society of Cosmetic Chemists of Japan. 1990;23:316–319.
denda1990facial.what: A-mode ultrasound of the forehead and the cheek in 63 men and 111 women by decade of age: forehead skin thickness 1.75 − 0.00376 × age mm in men (not significant) and 1.45 − 0.00412 × age mm in women (r = −0.36); thicker in men at every age.

derigal1989ultrasound.cite: de Rigal J, Escoffier C, Querleux B, et al.. Assessment of Aging of the Human Skin by In Vivo Ultrasonic Imaging. Journal of Investigative Dermatology. 1989;93:621–625.
derigal1989ultrasound.what: 25 MHz ultrasound of the forearm in 142 women by decade from 0–10 to 80–90 years: the ventral skin thickness does not vary significantly between the first and the seventh decade and atrophy appears after the eighth; on the dorsal side atrophy after the seventh decade.

dilger2025concentration.cite: Dilger OB, Carstens MF, Garrett DJ, et al.. Temporal- and concentration-dependent effects of transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-β1) in primary human knee fibroblasts. Bone & Joint Research. 2025;14:527–538.
dilger2025concentration.what: In primary human knee fibroblasts, collagen deposition was consistent across 0.5–40 ng/mL TGF-β1, while α-SMA protein and SMAD2 phosphorylation were induced at 1 ng/mL and robust ACTA2 transcription required 5 ng/mL.

dimri1995biomarker.cite: Dimri GP, Lee X, Basile G, et al.. A biomarker that identifies senescent human cells in culture and in aging skin in vivo.. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 1995;92:9363–9367.
dimri1995biomarker.what: In skin from 20 donors aged 20–90 y, SA-β-gal staining of dermal cells was absent in all young (< 40 y) donors and present in all but one old (> 69 y) donor; the grade counts positive cells, not a share.

diridollou2001ageing.cite: Diridollou S, Vabre V, Berson M, et al.. Skin ageing: changes of physical properties of human skin in vivo. International Journal of Cosmetic Science. 2001;23:353–362.
diridollou2001ageing.what: 20 MHz ultrasound of the volar forearm in 206 volunteers aged 6 months to 90 years: skin thickness rises from 0 to 20 years (0.7 mm + 0.009 mm × age in girls, 0.7 mm + 0.01 mm × age in boys) and falls after 60 years, especially in women (1.3 mm − 0.006 mm × age).

donnelly2010geometry.cite: Donnelly RF, Garland MJ, Morrow DIJ, et al.. Optical coherence tomography is a valuable tool in the study of the effects of microneedle geometry on skin penetration characteristics and in-skin dissolution. Journal of Controlled Release. 2010;147:333–341.
donnelly2010geometry.what: Measured by optical coherence tomography in porcine skin, 600 µm polymeric microneedles penetrated 330 µm at 4.4 N per array and 520 µm at 16.4 N; needle interspacing did not change the depth.

escoffier1989mechanical.cite: Escoffier C, de Rigal J, Rochefort A, et al.. Age-related mechanical properties of human skin: An in vivo study. Journal of Investigative Dermatology. 1989;93:353–357.
escoffier1989mechanical.what: Ultrasound of the ventral forearm in 54 men and 69 women by 10-year groups: skin thickness rises between 0 and 20–30 years (0.7 + 0.008 × age mm) and then falls, in women 0.89 − 0.003 × age, in men 1.05 − 0.004 × age mm; no variation between 15 and 65 years in the analysis of variance, thinner before and after.

farrokhi2022rejection.cite: Farrokhi A, Rahavi M, Jo S, et al.. Inflammatory Immune Responses Trigger Rejection of Allogeneic Fibroblasts Transplanted into Mouse Skin. Cell Transplantation. 2022;31:09636897221113803.
farrokhi2022rejection.what: Allogeneic fibroblasts injected intradermally were rejected one week after transplantation in immunocompetent mice; rejection did not occur in γ-chain-deficient NOD-SCID mice.

firooz2017echodensity.cite: Firooz A, Rajabi‐Estarabadi A, Zartab H, et al.. The influence of gender and age on the thickness and echo‐density of skin. Skin Research and Technology. 2017;23:13–20.
firooz2017echodensity.what: 22 and 50 MHz ultrasound in 30 healthy volunteers (17 women, 13 men, 24–61 years) at cheek, neck, palm, dorsal foot and sole: the dermis was thicker in men (significant at the neck and the dorsum of the foot) and its echo-density higher in women at all sites (significant at the neck); overall, skin thickness decreased with age.

francis1997distances.cite: Francis K, Palsson BO. Effective intercellular communication distances are determined by the relative time constants for cyto/chemokine secretion and diffusion. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 1997;94:12258–12262.
francis1997distances.what: A single cell communicates by a soluble signal within a domain of about 250 µm, within 10–30 min; one dimensionless group governs it.

gambichler2006epidermis.cite: Gambichler T, Matip R, Moussa G, et al.. In vivo data of epidermal thickness evaluated by optical coherence tomography: Effects of age, gender, skin type, and anatomic site. Journal of Dermatological Science. 2006;44:145–152.
gambichler2006epidermis.what: Optical coherence tomography of the epidermis at six sites in 71 Caucasians aged 20–40 or 60–80 years: thinner in the older group at every site (forearm 71.8 ± 10 against 60.8 ± 7.4 µm), no difference between the sexes except on the forehead of the older group, none by skin type.

ghahary1998igf1.cite: Ghahary A, Shen Q, Shen YJ, et al.. Induction of transforming growth factor β1 by insulin-like growth factor-1 in dermal fibroblasts. Journal of Cellular Physiology. 1998;174:301–309.
ghahary1998igf1.what: A TGF-β-specific ELISA on conditioned medium of human dermal fibroblasts gave 4.8 ± 0.8 pg per 10⁴ cells untreated and 12.3 ± 1.6 pg per 10⁴ cells after IGF-1 (n = 7, P < 0.05), confirmed by a mink lung growth-inhibition assay; the collection interval is not stated in the abstract.

gunin2011dermis.cite: Gunin AG, Kornilova NK, Vasilieva OV, et al.. Age-Related Changes in Proliferation, the Numbers of Mast Cells, Eosinophils, and cd45-Positive Cells in Human Dermis. The Journals of Gerontology Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences. 2011;66A:385–392.
gunin2011dermis.what: Fibroblast-like cells per mm² of dermis in 341 autopsy specimens of the frontal lower neck, from 20 weeks of pregnancy to 85 years: read off the bars about 4000 at 1–10 years, 2200 at 11–20 and 2100 to 2500 in every group up to 71–85 years; correlation with age over all cases r = −.58.

gupta2012anesthesia.cite: Gupta J, Denson DD, Felner EI, et al.. Rapid Local Anesthesia in Humans Using Minimally Invasive Microneedles. The Clinical Journal of Pain. 2012;28:129–135.
gupta2012anesthesia.what: Hollow microneedles 500 µm long injected lidocaine into the forearm of 15 participants and produced dermal anaesthesia equivalent to a 26-gauge intradermal needle.

hachmo2021papillary.cite: Hachmo Y, Hadanny A, Mendelovic S, et al.. The effect of hyperbaric oxygen therapy on the pathophysiology of skin aging: a prospective clinical trial. Aging. 2021;13:24500–24510.
hachmo2021papillary.what: Papillary dermis thickness measured on trichrome-stained punch biopsies of post-auricular skin in 13 healthy men aged 68.1 ± 2.5 y was 133.22 ± 22.42 µm at baseline (N = 11), with an epidermis of 55.88 ± 9.19 µm.

hanasono2003fibroblasts.cite: Hanasono MM, Kita M, Mikulec AA, et al.. Autocrine Growth Factor Production by Fetal, Keloid, and Normal Dermal Fibroblasts. Archives of Facial Plastic Surgery. 2003;5:26–30.
hanasono2003fibroblasts.what: Normal adult, fetal and keloid dermal fibroblasts (one cell line each) were cultured serum-free and supernatants collected at 4, 24 and 72 h; TGF-β1 per viable cell by ELISA was higher in fetal (5 to 7 times) and keloid than in normal adult cells at 24 and 72 h. The values exist only in Fig. 1, as "pg/mL per cell" without cell count or well volume, so there is no secretion rate (claim R23).

herbig2006primates.cite: Herbig U, Ferreira M, Condel L, et al.. Cellular Senescence in Aging Primates. Science. 2006;311:1257–1257.
herbig2006primates.what: In skin biopsies of 30 baboons aged 5–30 y, dermal fibroblast nuclei with telomere-dysfunction-induced foci reached 15–20 % at 25–30 y; the authors conclude that senescent cells can account for more than 15 % of the cells of aged animals.

hebda1999transplanted.cite: Hebda PA, Dohar JE. Transplanted fetal fibroblasts: Survival and distribution over time in normal adult dermis compared with autogenic, allogenic, and xenogenic adult fibroblasts. Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery. 1999;121:245–251.
hebda1999transplanted.what: Labelled fibroblasts injected intradermally into adult rabbit skin followed a biphasic curve — a rise and fall in cell density over 0–28 days, then a slow decrease — and were still detectable at 56 days, without signs of rejection.

hoffmann1994sonography.cite: Hoffmann K, Stuücker M, Dirschka T, et al.. Twenty MHz B‐scan sonography for visualization and skin thickness measurement of human skin. Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology. 1994;3:302–313.
hoffmann1994sonography.what: 20 MHz B-scan of 51 skin sites in 20 men and 20 women aged 15–76 years (median 32 and 47): corium (dermis) by sex at 21 sites of head and neck, e.g. forehead 2.23 and 1.90 mm, cheek 2.23 and 1.84, upper eyelid 0.59 and 0.64, chin 3.04 and 2.69 mm; thinner in women at all sites but two; the entry echo is wider than the epidermis; the corium cannot be measured at the lateral angle of the eye and the wing and bridge of the nose.

idda2020senescence.cite: Idda ML, McClusky WG, Lodde V, et al.. Survey of senescent cell markers with age in human tissues. Aging. 2020;12:4052–4066.
idda2020senescence.what: In human dermis p21-positive cells increased with age, up to 15 % of cells in donors over 65; p16 was almost undetectable in the dermis.

ince2015dermal.cite: Ince B, Dadaci M, Oltulu P, et al.. Effect of Dermal Thickness on Scars in Women with Type III–IV Fitzpatrick Skin. Aesthetic Plastic Surgery. 2015;39:318–324.
ince2015dermal.what: Breast skin of 50 Turkish women of Fitzpatrick type III–IV, 33 of them type IV: dermal thickness 4.99 mm on average, not associated with the skin type.

jeong2023facial.cite: Jeong KM, Seo JY, Kim A, et al.. Ultrasonographic analysis of facial skin thickness in relation to age, site, sex, and body mass index. Skin Research and Technology. 2023;29:e13426.
jeong2023facial.what: Ultrasound at eight facial points in 99 adults aged 19 to 71 years: the dermis of the glabella and the lateral forehead correlates weakly and negatively with age, that of the central forehead does not.

jeyapalan2007primates.cite: Jeyapalan JC, Ferreira M, Sedivy JM, et al.. Accumulation of senescent cells in mitotic tissue of aging primates. Mechanisms of Ageing and Development. 2007;128:36–44.
jeyapalan2007primates.what: In baboon skin, dermal fibroblasts with damaged telomeres accumulate with age and reach over 15 % of all fibroblasts.

kelley1993autoinduction.cite: Kelley J, Shull S, Walsh JJ, et al.. Auto-induction of Transforming Growth Factor- β in Human Lung Fibroblasts. American Journal of Respiratory Cell and Molecular Biology. 1993;8:417–424.
kelley1993autoinduction.what: Human fetal lung fibroblasts (IMR90) accumulated TGF-β in conditioned medium at 90 ± 7 pg/10⁶ cells/h after a brief TGF-β1 exposure, against ≤ 15 pg/10⁶ cells/h uninduced, for up to 72 h; as little as 1 ng/mL auto-induced secretion.

klingberg2014prestress.cite: Klingberg F, Chow ML, Koehler A, et al.. Prestress in the extracellular matrix sensitizes latent TGF-β1 for activation. Journal of Cell Biology. 2014;207:283–297.
klingberg2014prestress.what: In primary human dermal fibroblasts, active TGF-β1 was ≤ 2 % of total at baseline, rising to 11 % on thrombin-induced contraction and to 36 % in dermal myofibroblasts.

korzekwa2025face.cite: Korzekwa S, Matusz K, Kukulski M, et al.. Quantitative Analysis of the Human Face Skin Thickness—A High-Frequency Ultrasound Study. Journal of Clinical Medicine. 2025;14:8401.
korzekwa2025face.what: 75 MHz ultrasound at 38 facial sites in 45 patients aged 22–73 years: location explains the skin thickness, age has only a modest effect, and a progressive thinning with age was not confirmed.

kretsos2008dermis.cite: Kretsos K, Miller MA, Zamora-Estrada G, et al.. Partitioning, diffusivity and clearance of skin permeants in mammalian dermis. International Journal of Pharmaceutics. 2008;346:64–79.
kretsos2008dermis.what: Decay lengths of topically applied small permeants in dermis 210–920 µm (capillary clearance 0.9–14 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹).

lagarrigue2012papilla.cite: Lagarrigue SG, George J, Questel E, et al.. In vivo quantification of epidermis pigmentation and dermis papilla density with reflectance confocal microscopy: variations with age and skin phototype. Experimental Dermatology. 2012;21:281–286.
lagarrigue2012papilla.what: Reflectance confocal microscopy of 111 women of phototypes I–VI: dermal papillae per image 3.6 in types I–II and 7.1 in V–VI, falling with age, by 83 % in types I–II and 36 % in V–VI between 18–25 and above 65 years.

langton2017dermal.cite: Langton AK, Graham HK, McConnell JC, et al.. Organization of the dermal matrix impacts the biomechanical properties of skin. British Journal of Dermatology. 2017;177:818–827.
langton2017dermal.what: Young black African or African-Caribbean (phototype VI) against white Northern European (phototypes I–II) volunteers: the dermal–epidermal junction is more convoluted in the black skin, most at the sun-exposed forearm.

langton2019color.cite: Langton AK, Alessi S, Hann M, et al.. Aging in Skin of Color: Disruption to Elastic Fiber Organization Is Detrimental to Skin’s Biomechanical Function. Journal of Investigative Dermatology. 2019;139:779–788.
langton2019color.what: Black African-American volunteers of phototype V–VI, young and aged: the epidermis thins and the junction flattens with age, less at the protected buttock.

lasagni1995echographic.cite: Lasagni C, Seidenari S. Echographic assessment of age‐dependent variations of skin thickness. Skin Research and Technology. 1995;1:81–85.
lasagni1995echographic.what: 20 MHz ultrasound of 162 subjects aged 27 to 90 years at six sites: skin thickness 1.48, 1.42, 1.48 and 1.42 mm at 27–31, 40–50, 60–70 and 70–90 years, the last significantly lower; men 1.55, women 1.37 mm.

laurent2007needlelength.cite: Laurent A, Mistretta F, Bottigioli D, et al.. Echographic measurement of skin thickness in adults by high frequency ultrasound to assess the appropriate microneedle length for intradermal delivery of vaccines. Vaccine. 2007;25:6423–6430.
laurent2007needlelength.what: 20 MHz ultrasound in 342 adults: mean skin thickness (epidermis plus dermis) 2.02 mm at the deltoid and 1.91 mm at the waist; the authors conclude a 1.5 mm needle inserted perpendicularly reaches the dermis regardless of gender, age, ethnicity and body mass index.

liao2026chromatin.cite: Liao Y, Yuan L, Sornapudi TR, et al.. Chromatin accessibility regulates age-dependent nuclear mechanotransduction. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 2026;123:e2522217123.
liao2026chromatin.what: Young dermal fibroblasts respond synergistically to tension plus TGF-β; in aged cells the response is blunted or divergent, in line with chromatin accessibility. Cells were stimulated with 10 ng/mL TGF-β (a dose, not a threshold).

lichtman2016isoforms.cite: Lichtman MK, Otero‐Vinas M, Falanga V. Transforming growth factor beta (TGF‐β) isoforms in wound healing and fibrosis. Wound Repair and Regeneration. 2016;24:215–222.
lichtman2016isoforms.what: Review: TGF-β1 may mediate fibrosis in adult wounds, while TGF-β3 may promote scarless healing in the fetus and reduced scarring in adults.

lin2002ultrathick.cite: Lin CH, Lee GB, Chang BW, et al.. A new fabrication process for ultra-thick microfluidic microstructures utilizing SU-8 photoresist. Journal of Micromechanics and Microengineering. 2002;12:590–597.
lin2002ultrathick.what: A constant-volume-injection coating gave SU-8 50 films up to 1.5 mm thick in a single coating, measured at 494.32 ± 17.13 µm for a nominal 500 µm film (n = 7), uniform to better than 3.1 % over 10 × 10 cm².

lintzeri2022epidermis.cite: Lintzeri DA, Karimian N, Blume‐Peytavi U, et al.. Epidermal thickness in healthy humans: a systematic review and meta‐analysis. Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology. 2022;36:1191–1200.
lintzeri2022epidermis.what: Systematic review and meta-analysis of the epidermal thickness of healthy humans (142 studies, 37 skin areas): histology, optical coherence tomography and laser scanning microscopy agree, high-frequency ultrasound reads systematically higher and should not be used; the epidermis is thinner in the older group at all ten areas compared (volar forearm 80.6 µm at a mean age of 27.1 and 63.6 µm at 60.0 years); no influence of sex.

lovell1987collagen.cite: Lovell CR, Smolenski KA, Duance VC, et al.. Type I and III collagen content and fibre distribution in normal human skin during ageing. British Journal of Dermatology. 1987;117:419–428.
lovell1987collagen.what: Abdominal skin of 30 subjects aged 0 to 90 years: the collagen concentration does not vary with age; type III is 18 to 21.5 % of types I plus III between 14 and 65 years and more variable, up to 31 %, from 65 years.

marcosgarces2014collagen.cite: Marcos‐Garcés V, Molina Aguilar P, Bea Serrano C, et al.. Age‐related dermal collagen changes during development, maturation and ageing – a morphometric and comparative study. Journal of Anatomy. 2014;225:98–108.
marcosgarces2014collagen.what: In 45 autopsy samples of periumbilical skin the width of the papillary dermis (thin-bundle layer, set against the thick reticular bundles) rose linearly with age, 63.24 µm at birth with 0.361 µm per year (R² = 0.26), while the area occupied by collagen and the thickness of collagen bundles fell with age in the papillary dermis; the authors attribute the thickening to water and dermatan sulphate.

martanto2006microinfusion.cite: Martanto W, Moore JS, Kashlan O, et al.. Microinfusion Using Hollow Microneedles. Pharmaceutical Research. 2006;23:104–113.
martanto2006microinfusion.what: Single hollow glass microneedles inserted 720–1080 µm into human cadaver skin infused 15–96 µL/h, rising to 1130 µL/h once the flow resistance of compressed dermal tissue was relieved.

mata2006multilayer.cite: Mata A, Fleischman AJ, Roy S. Fabrication of multi-layer SU-8 microstructures. Journal of Micromechanics and Microengineering. 2006;16:276–284.
mata2006multilayer.what: Multi-level SU-8 microstructures were built from up to six alternating thin and thick layers with a single development step, reaching overall thicknesses up to 500 µm with a minimum lateral feature size of 10 µm.

mccollum2011avotermin.cite: McCollum PT, Bush JA, James G, et al.. Randomized phase II clinical trial of avotermin versus placebo for scar improvement. British Journal of Surgery. 2011;98:925–934.
mccollum2011avotermin.what: TGF-β3 (avotermin) 500 ng per 100 µL per linear cm of wound margin improved scar appearance in a phase II trial (n = 156).

meng2022facial.cite: Meng Y, Feng L, Shan J, et al.. Application of high-frequency ultrasound to assess facial skin thickness in association with gender, age, and BMI in healthy adults. BMC Medical Imaging. 2022;22:113.
meng2022facial.what: 24 MHz ultrasound at eight facial sites in 118 adults: forehead dermis 1.17 mm in men and 0.86 mm in women; in women it falls with age (r = −0.284), in men it does not.

mercurio2016brazilian.cite: Mercurio DG, Jdid R, Morizot F, et al.. Morphological, structural and biophysical properties of French and Brazilian photoaged skin. British Journal of Dermatology. 2016;174:553–561.
mercurio2016brazilian.what: 41 French and 41 Brazilian women aged 40–65 years, confocal microscopy and ultrasound at the face and the forearm: viable epidermis and dermis not significantly different between the two groups.

miller2003density.cite: Miller CC, Godeau G, Lebreton‐DeCoster C, et al.. Validation of a morphometric method for evaluating fibroblast numbers in normal and pathologic tissues. Experimental Dermatology. 2003;12:403–411.
miller2003density.what: Mid-dermis fibroblast counts of 2100–4100 per mm³ in normal donors.

monnier2020lcoct.cite: Monnier J, Tognetti L, Miyamoto M, et al.. Invivocharacterization of healthy human skin with a novel, non‐invasive imaging technique: line‐field confocal optical coherence tomography. Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology. 2020;34:2914–2921.
monnier2020lcoct.what: Line-field confocal OCT of 29 young volunteers at seven sites: no papillae on the cheek and the nose of any of them, the cheek a flat dermal–epidermal junction; clear papillae on the forearm in half of them.

muizzuddin2010barrier.cite: Muizzuddin N, Hellemans L, Van Overloop L, et al.. Structural and functional differences in barrier properties of African American, Caucasian and East Asian skin. Journal of Dermatological Science. 2010;59:123–128.
muizzuddin2010barrier.what: Barrier of the cheek and arm in 73 African American (pigment type IV–VI), 119 Caucasian (II–III) and 149 East Asian (III–IV) women aged 18–45 years.

munavalli2013azficel.cite: Munavalli GS, Smith S, Maslowski JM, et al.. Successful Treatment of Depressed, Distensible Acne Scars Using Autologous Fibroblasts: A Multi-Site, Prospective, Double Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial. Dermatologic Surgery. 2013;39:1226–1236.
munavalli2013azficel.what: Three intradermal sessions, 14 ± 3 days apart, of at most 2 mL autologous fibroblast suspension at 10–20 million cells per mL (n = 99); mean total dose 5.9 mL per cheek. The azficel-T label (claim P20) has 3–6 week intervals.

nakerakanti2011ccn2.cite: Nakerakanti SS, Bujor AM, Trojanowska M. CCN2 Is Required for the TGF-β Induced Activation of Smad1 - Erk1/2 Signaling Network. PLoS ONE. 2011;6:e21911.
nakerakanti2011ccn2.what: CCN2/CTGF stimulated collagen gene expression below 50 ng/mL and inhibited it at higher doses: a window with a lower and an upper side.

needleman1990fibroblasts.cite: Needleman BW, Choi J, Burrows‐Mezu A, et al.. Secretion and binding of transforming growth factor β by scleroderma and normal dermal fibroblasts. Arthritis & Rheumatism. 1990;33:650–656.
needleman1990fibroblasts.what: Human dermal fibroblasts: 12 431 ± 2425 TGF-β receptors per cell with a K_d of 27.1 ± 5.2 pM (normal donors), and a 24-hour secretion of 29.7 ± 5.8 pmol/10⁶ cells (means ± SEM).

neerken2004oct.cite: Neerken S, Lucassen GW, Bisschop MA, et al.. Characterization of age-related effects in human skin: A comparative study that applies confocal laser scanning microscopy and optical coherence tomography. Journal of Biomedical Optics. 2004;9:274–281.
neerken2004oct.what: Confocal microscopy and OCT of the forearm and the temple in 15 volunteers aged 19–24 and 15 aged 54–57 years: the epidermis above the papillae is 47 and 50 µm thick on the forearm, the epidermis to the base of the rete ridges 89 and 75 µm; the dermal–epidermal junction flattens.

oyleryaniv2017niches.cite: Oyler-Yaniv A, Oyler-Yaniv J, Whitlock BM, et al.. A Tunable Diffusion-Consumption Mechanism of Cytokine Propagation Enables Plasticity in Cell-to-Cell Communication in the Immune System. Immunity. 2017;46:609–620.
oyleryaniv2017niches.what: Cytokine diffusion and consumption make niches with sharp boundaries whose size scales with the density of consuming cells; in vivo interactions over 80–120 µm.

ozawa2004vegf.cite: Ozawa CR, Banfi A, Glazer NL, et al.. Microenvironmental VEGF concentration, not total dose, determines a threshold between normal and aberrant angiogenesis. Journal of Clinical Investigation. 2004;113:516–527.
ozawa2004vegf.what: The local amount of VEGF secreted, not the total dose, decides between normal and aberrant angiogenesis; clones secreting about 5–70 ng/10⁶ cells/day in culture gave normal vessels, about 100 and above gave hemangiomas (threshold between 70 and 100).

pedrazzani2020lcoct.cite: Pedrazzani M, Breugnot J, Rouaud‐Tinguely P, et al.. Comparison of line‐field confocal optical coherence tomography images with histological sections: Validation of a new method for in vivo and non‐invasive quantification of superficial dermis thickness. Skin Research and Technology. 2020;26:398–404.
pedrazzani2020lcoct.what: LC-OCT in vivo on the cheeks of 36 Caucasian women: the thickness of the superficial dermis (DEJ to the next intensity maximum, 2 µm resolution) fell 45 % from 94.4 ± 18.5 µm at 22–27 y to 52.4 ± 13.9 µm at 61–69 y. Ex vivo it equals the layer of dense thin fibres under the DEJ (80 ± 7 against 81 ± 16 µm) and not the depth to the vascular plexus (330 ± 26 µm).

pellacani1999facial.cite: Pellacani G, Seidenari S. Variations in facial skin thickness and echogenicity with site and age. Acta dermato-venereologica. 1999;79:366–9.
pellacani1999facial.what: 20 MHz ultrasound at 12 facial sites in 20 women aged 25–30 and 20 aged 60–90 years: the skin is thicker in the elderly on the forehead, cheeks, lips, chin and nose, significantly on the lateral forehead, lips and nose; on some facial areas the border between dermis and hypodermis cannot be delineated.

petrof2013erosions.cite: Petrof G, Martinez-Queipo M, Mellerio JE, et al.. Fibroblast cell therapy enhances initial healing in recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa wounds: results of a randomized, vehicle-controlled trial. British Journal of Dermatology. 2013;169:1025–1033.
petrof2013erosions.what: One intradermal injection of 5 × 10⁶ allogeneic fibroblasts per linear cm of wound margin increased the healing rate of RDEB erosions within the first 28 days but not thereafter.

quaglino1996dermis.cite: Quaglino D, Bergamini G, Boraldi F, et al.. Ultrastructural and morphometrical evaluations on normal human dermal connective tissue--the influence of age, sex and body region. The British journal of dermatology. 1996;134:1013–22.
quaglino1996dermis.what: Ultrastructure and morphometry of dermal biopsies from 50 healthy Caucasian subjects (6 fetal months to 83 years): only slight or negligible differences between males and females for collagen, elastic fibres and mesenchymal cells.

quan2002uv.cite: Quan T, He T, Kang S, et al.. Ultraviolet Irradiation Alters Transforming Growth Factor β/Smad Pathway in Human Skin In Vivo. Journal of Investigative Dermatology. 2002;119:499–506.
quan2002uv.what: Sun-protected adult human skin expresses TGF-β1, β2 and β3 transcripts in a ratio of 1:5:3.

querleux2009ethnic.cite: Querleux B, Baldeweck T, Diridollou S, et al.. Skin from various ethnic origins and aging: an in vivo cross‐sectional multimodality imaging study. Skin Research and Technology. 2009;15:306–313.
querleux2009ethnic.what: In about 400 women of four ethnic groups, papillary dermis thickness appeared quite constant irrespective of age or ethnic group.

raphael2013depth.cite: Raphael AP, Meliga SC, Chen X, et al.. Depth-resolved characterization of diffusion properties within and across minimally-perturbed skin layers. Journal of Controlled Release. 2013;166:87–94.
raphael2013depth.what: Diffusivity of 70 kDa and 2 MDa rhodamine-dextrans in mouse skin in vivo was low in the epidermis and increased by about an order of magnitude through the dermis, which the authors attribute to pores enlarging from papillary to reticular dermis.

ressler2006p16.cite: Ressler S, Bartkova J, Niederegger H, et al.. p16 INK4A is a robust in vivo biomarker of cellular aging in human skin. Aging Cell. 2006;5:379–389.
ressler2006p16.what: p16INK4A-positive cells in healthy human skin by age group (0–20, 21–70, 71–95 y; three biopsies each): 0.0, 3.1 and 8.2 per dermal field of 0.16 × 0.21 mm (P < 0.001), with no change in cell density; also higher in the epidermis.

roh2022heights.cite: Roh H, Yoon YJ, Park JS, et al.. Fabrication of High-Density Out-of-Plane Microneedle Arrays with Various Heights and Diverse Cross-Sectional Shapes. Nano-Micro Letters. 2022;14:24.
roh2022heights.what: One photolithography step followed by two deep-reactive-ion-etch steps gave silicon microneedle arrays with heights from 68.54 to 246.44 µm within a single photomask design, densities up to 625 needles/mm² and aspect ratios up to about 25.

romgens2014tip.cite: Römgens AM, Bader DL, Bouwstra JA, et al.. Monitoring the penetration process of single microneedles with varying tip diameters. Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials. 2014;40:397–405.
romgens2014tip.what: Single solid microneedles with tip diameters of 5–37 µm inserted into human ex vivo skin needed 20–167 mN, rising linearly with tip diameter; the force drop occurred at about 160 µm depth for every tip diameter.

romgens2015diffusion.cite: Römgens AM, Bader DL, Bouwstra JA, et al.. Diffusion profile of macromolecules within and between human skin layers for (trans)dermal drug delivery. Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials. 2015;50:215–222.
romgens2015diffusion.what: FRAP in human skin: median dermal diffusion coefficient 23 µm²/s for 40 kDa dextran (9 µm²/s for 500 kDa), with only marginal differences between papillary and reticular dermis.

roy2024implanting.cite: Roy B, Pekec T, Yuan L, et al.. Implanting mechanically reprogrammed fibroblasts for aged tissue regeneration and wound healing. Aging Cell. 2024;23:e14032.
roy2024implanting.what: Spheroids equivalent to 40,000 cells in 50 µL per implantation site, 2–3 sites per reconstructed aged skin model, within the 2-mm-deep dermis, analysed after 10 days. Matrix deposition of the implanted cells declined after 2–3 divisions; the authors note it could also indicate fibrotic activation.

sandbymoller2003epidermis.cite: Sandby-Møller J, Poulsen T, Wulf HC. Epidermal Thickness at Different Body Sites: Relationship to Age, Gender, Pigmentation, Blood Content, Skin Type and Smoking Habits. Acta Dermato-Venereologica. 2003;83:410–413.
sandbymoller2003epidermis.what: Biopsies from three body sites of 71 volunteers, measured microscopically: stratum corneum 18.3 ± 4.9 µm and cellular epidermis 56.6 ± 11.5 µm at the dorsal forearm (shoulder 11.0 and 70.3 µm, buttock 14.9 and 81.5 µm). Body site explains most of the variation.

sauermann2002clsm.cite: Sauermann K, Clemann S, Jaspers S, et al.. Age related changes of human skin investigated with histometric measurements by confocal laser scanning microscopy in vivo. Skin Research and Technology. 2002;8:52–56.
sauermann2002clsm.what: Confocal microscopy of the volar forearm in 13 volunteers aged 18–25 and 13 over 65 years: 40.56 against 13.82 dermal papillae per mm², the epidermis above the papillae 35.5 against 40.0 µm.

seidenari1994echography.cite: Seidenari S, Pagnoni A, Di Nardo A, et al.. Echographic evaluation with image analysis of normal skin: variations according to age and sex. Skin pharmacology : the official journal of the Skin Pharmacology Society. 1994;7:201–9.
seidenari1994echography.what: 20 MHz ultrasound at six sites in 24 subjects aged 27–31 and 24 over 60 years: the skin is thinner in the elderly except at the lower back in men and the volar forearm in women, significantly at four of twelve comparisons; thicker in men except at the lower back of the young.

seidenari2000children.cite: Seidenari S, Giusti G, Bertoni L, et al.. Thickness and Echogenicity of the Skin in Children as Assessed by 20-MHz Ultrasound. Dermatology. 2000;201:218–222.
seidenari2000children.what: 20 MHz ultrasound at eight sites in 42 children aged 2–13 and 30 adults aged 25–40 years: the children's skin is thinner at every site (volar forearm 1.01 ± 0.16 against 1.30 ± 0.24 mm) and thickens with age.

serpero2006polyp.cite: Serpero L, Petecchia L, Sabatini F, et al.. The effect of transforming growth factor (TGF)-β1 and (TGF)-β2 on nasal polyp fibroblast activities involved upper airway remodeling: Modulation by fluticasone propionate. Immunology Letters. 2006;105:61–67.
serpero2006polyp.what: Nasal-polyp fibroblasts stimulated with 1, 10 and 20 ng/mL TGF-β1 or TGF-β2: α-SMA rose significantly only at the two highest doses, while 1 ng/mL TGF-β1 already raised proliferation.

shuster1975collagen.cite: Shuster S, Black MM, McVITIE E. The influence of age and sex on skin thickness, skin collagen and density. British Journal of Dermatology. 1975;93:639–643.
shuster1975collagen.what: Forearm skin collagen decreased with age and was less in females at all ages; skin collagen and dermal thickness are directly related.

sprugel1987kinetics.cite: Sprugel KH, McPherson JM, Clowes AW, et al.. Effects of growth factors in vivo. I. Cell ingrowth into porous subcutaneous chambers. The American journal of pathology. 1987;129:601–13.
sprugel1987kinetics.what: ¹²⁵I-TGF-β was cleared from subcutaneous collagen chambers in rats with an initial-phase half-life of 22 h.

strasen2018variability.cite: Strasen J, Sarma U, Jentsch M, et al.. Cell‐specific responses to the cytokine TGFβ are determined by variability in protein levels. Molecular Systems Biology. 2018;14:MSB177733.
strasen2018variability.what: The response of a single cell to a given TGF-β dose is set cell by cell by the levels of defined signalling proteins.

takahashi2016exposure.cite: Takahashi H, Jung Heo Y, Arakawa N, et al.. Scalable fabrication of microneedle arrays via spatially controlled UV exposure. Microsystems & Nanoengineering. 2016;2:16049.
takahashi2016exposure.what: Inclined and rotated UV lithography through circular mask patterns forms needle-shaped exposure-dose distributions in a negative epoxy resist, so needle heights and contours can be varied from the same mask patterns by the inclination angle and dose; heights of 330–900 µm at a 1200 µm pitch were made, with tip radii of curvature of 12 µm.

takema1994facial.cite: Takema Y, Yorimoto Y, Kawai M, et al.. Age-related changes in the elastic properties and thickness of human facial skin. British Journal of Dermatology. 1994;131:641–648.
takema1994facial.what: 20 MHz ultrasound in 170 women aged 17 to 76 years by decade: forearm skin thins with age (1.06 to 0.86 mm, r = −0.567), the skin of the forehead and the cheek thickens.

tan1982ultrasound.cite: Tan CY, Statham B, Marks R, et al.. Skin thickness measurement by pulsed ultrasound: its reproducibility, validation and variability. British Journal of Dermatology. 1982;106:657–667.
tan1982ultrasound.what: Pulsed-ultrasound skin thickness (epidermis and dermis) of the flexor forearm against age: males over 21 years 1.11 − 0.0036 × age mm (r = −0.52, n = 99), females over 21 years 0.86 − 0.002 × age mm (r = −0.38, n = 119); up to 20 years, both sexes, 0.54 + 0.019 × age mm (r = 0.77, n = 43).

taylor2002color.cite: Taylor SC. Skin of color: Biology, structure, function, and implications for dermatologic disease. Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology. 2002;46:S41–S62.
taylor2002color.what: Review of skin of colour: the Fitzpatrick phototype system rates skin by its reaction to sunlight and correlates its colour with burning or tanning; developed for white skin; skin of colour divided into types IV (olive), V (brown) and VI (black), which rarely or never burn and tan readily.

urban2023isoforms.cite: Urban L, Čoma M, Lacina L, et al.. Heterogeneous response to TGF-β1/3 isoforms in fibroblasts of different origins: implications for wound healing and tumorigenesis. Histochemistry and Cell Biology. 2023;160:541–554.
urban2023isoforms.what: In fibroblasts of different origins, TGF-β1 activated signalling more potently than TGF-β3; TGF-β3 was rather inhibitory in keloid- and hypertrophic-scar-derived fibroblasts.

verbaan2007arrays.cite: Verbaan FJ, Bal SM, van den Berg DJ, et al.. Assembled microneedle arrays enhance the transport of compounds varying over a large range of molecular weight across human dermatomed skin. Journal of Controlled Release. 2007;117:238–245.
verbaan2007arrays.what: Assembled hollow metal microneedle arrays pierced dermatomed human skin at needle lengths of 900, 700 and 550 µm, while 300 µm needles did not.

waaijer2012morphometric.cite: Waaijer MEC, Gunn DA, Catt SD, et al.. Morphometric skin characteristics dependent on chronological and biological age: the Leiden Longevity Study. AGE. 2012;34:1543–1552.
waaijer2012morphometric.what: Biopsies of the sun-protected inner upper arm of 286 persons aged 44 to 81 years: epidermal thickness 42.4, 42.6, 40.2 and 38.2 µm by age quartile, with a flattening of the epidermis.

wang2023density.cite: Wang S, Yu R, Fan W, et al.. Detection of skin thickness and density in healthy Chinese people by using high‐frequency ultrasound. Skin Research and Technology. 2023;29:e13219.
wang2023density.what: 22 or 75 MHz ultrasound at 13 sites in 189 healthy Chinese volunteers (85 men, 104 women, 22–75 years): the dermis was thicker in men at most sites, the density of epidermis and dermis lower in men at most sites, and dermis thickness and density lower in the older group at almost all sites.

vitellaro1994stereology.cite: Vitellaro‐Zuccarello L, Cappelletti S, Rossi VDP, et al.. Stereological analysis of collagen and elastic fibers in the normal human dermis: Variability with age, sex, and body region. The Anatomical Record. 1994;238:153–162.
vitellaro1994stereology.what: Stereology of skin biopsies from trunk or limbs (26 males, 19 females): the fractional volume of collagen fibres is constant through the dermis layers and always higher in females than in males, except in the second and third decades of life; collagen fibre density rises with age to 30–40 years and then falls.

wang2025ultrasound.cite: Wang Y, Tian M, Guo R, et al.. Quantification of normal skin thickness using very high-frequency ultrasound: a clinical study in Chinese adults. Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery. 2025;15:5218–5231.
wang2025ultrasound.what: 50 MHz ultrasound in 74 healthy adults: abdominal epidermis 0.1100 ± 0.0178 mm, abdominal dermis 2.3919 ± 0.5431 mm, full-thickness abdominal skin 2.5130 ± 0.5383 mm.

wei2018microneedle.cite: Wei JCJ, Haridass IN, Crichton ML, et al.. Space- and time-resolved investigation on diffusion kinetics of human skin following macromolecule delivery by microneedle arrays. Scientific Reports. 2018;8:17759.
wei2018microneedle.what: Ex vivo human skin, 70–2000 kDa dextrans: dermal diffusivities 1–20 µm²/s, lowest at the dermal–epidermal junction (0.7–3 µm²/s).

whitmore2000caliper.cite: Whitmore SE, Sago NJG. Caliper-measured skin thickness is similar in white and black women. Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology. 2000;42:76–79.
whitmore2000caliper.what: Caliper skin thickness of the sun-protected volar forearm in 86 white and 40 black women aged 20–69 years: 1.41 against 1.39 mm, no difference by race in any age band or in the multivariate model.

williams2004postbake.cite: Williams JD, Wang W. Study on the postbaking process and the effects on UV lithography of high aspect ratio SU-8 microstructures. Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning, Materials, and Metrology. 2004;3:563–568.
williams2004postbake.what: Controlling internal stress during the post-exposure bake gave SU-8 aspect ratios up to 40:1 in isolated open-field structures 1–1.5 mm thick with a standard broadband UV source.

zi2011dynamics.cite: Zi Z, Feng Z, Chapnick DA, et al.. Quantitative analysis of transient and sustained transforming growth factor‐β signaling dynamics. Molecular Systems Biology. 2011;7:MSB201122.
zi2011dynamics.what: Ligand-induced short-term Smad2 phosphorylation is graded, whereas long-term Smad2 phosphorylation, long-term PAI-1 expression and the growth-inhibitory response are switch-like to a small change in TGF-β levels.
